question.text: A Cat II FPI investor has inadvertently breached the FPI ceiling limit in an Indian listed investee company of Lotus Capital AIF. Under Schedule I of FEMA NDI Rules, 2019, within what period must the FPI divest its excess holdings?

answer.text: Within 5 TRADING days from the date of settlement of the trades that caused the breach
No divestment required; pay penalty instead

explanation.text: The Logic: If an FPI breaches the FPI ceiling limit, the investor has 5 trading days from the date of settlement of the trades to divest its holdings in the company. The default aggregate FPI limit follows the applicable sectoral cap in Schedule I of the NDI Rules, and the aggregate FPI cap is 24% of paid-up equity (fully diluted) where FDI is prohibited. The Trap: Options A and C extend the cure window. Option D bypasses the divestment remedy. Note: Workbook pages 376-378 contain the FEMA/NDI FPI limit, breach-cure period and divestment discussion.
